CFML Language Reference: Functions

SetVariable

Sets the variable named by the first argument to the value of the second and returns that value. Because the name is an ordinary string, you can compute it at run time, for example from a loop counter or a query column.

Category

Dynamic evaluation functions

Syntax

SetVariable(name, value)

Parameters

name
A string containing the variable name, optionally with a scope or struct path, such as "Score_Ann", "Session.Cart" or "Totals.Sales".
value
The value to store. Any type is accepted.

Returns

The value that was assigned.

Usage

SetVariable is the write-side partner of Evaluate. Since 4.0 you can also write the same thing with a quoted name on the left of a CFSET, for example <CFSET "Score_#Name#" = 10>, but SetVariable works in any expression, including inside CFSCRIPT.

The name must be a valid variable name once the pound signs have been resolved: letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFQUERY NAME="Depts" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
SELECT Department, Count(*) AS Heads FROM Employees GROUP BY Department
</CFQUERY>
<!--- create one variable per department: Heads_Sales, Heads_Marketing ... --->
<CFLOOP QUERY="Depts">
  <CFSET Dummy = SetVariable("Heads_" & Department, Heads)>
</CFLOOP>
<CFOUTPUT>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>Variable</TH><TH>Value</TH></TR>
<CFLOOP QUERY="Depts">
<TR><TD>Heads_#Department#</TD><TD>#Evaluate("Heads_" & Department)#</TD></TR>
</CFLOOP>
</TABLE>
</CFOUTPUT>
